paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on how the students can contribute to a green campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设大学报纸正在邀请学生为其即将出版的报纸投稿，内容涉及学生如何为绿色校园做出贡献。您现在需要写一篇论文以供提交。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials such as silicone and are designed to imitate real human faces — down to every last detail.
paragraphs.translationZh: 超逼真的面具由硅胶等柔性材料制成，旨在模仿真实的人脸 - 精细到每一个细节。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a study by the Universities of York and Kyoto, researchers asked participants to look at pairs of photographs and decide which showed a 26 face and which showed a person wearing a mask.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在约克大学和京都大学的一项研究中，研究人员要求参与者观看几对照片，并决定哪一张是正常的面孔，哪一张是戴着面具的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Surprisingly, participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases.
paragraphs.translationZh: 令人惊讶的是，参与者在五分之一的情况下做出了错误的决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: The 20% error rate 27 in the study likely underestimates the extent to which people would struggle to tell an 28 face from the real thing outside of the lab.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究中观察到的 20% 错误率可能低估了人们在实验室外难以区分人造面孔和真实面孔的程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers collected data from participants from both the UK and Japan to 29 any differences according to race. When trial participants were asked to choose between photographs of faces of a different race from theirs, response times were slower and selections were 5% less 30 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员收集了来自英国和日本参与者的数据，以确定种族差异。当试验参与者被要求在与自己不同种族的面孔照片中进行选择时，反应时间会变慢，选择的准确性也会降低 5%。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are now dozens of criminal cases in which offenders have 31 themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender, sending police investigations down the wrong path.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在有数十起刑事案件，罪犯冒充不同年龄、种族或性别的人，导致警方的调查走上了错误的道路。

paragraphs.sourceText: In one recent case, an international gang used an 32 realistic mask to pose as a French minister, 33 business executives out of millions of pounds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近的一起案件中，一个国际团伙使用极其逼真的面具冒充法国部长，骗取企业高管数百万英镑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Dr Jet Sanders, who worked on the study while a PhD student at the University of York, said: “Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention as super realistic masks may 34 the key characteristics of a person’s appearance to be 35 identified.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 约克大学博士生杰特·桑德斯博士参与了这项研究，他表示：“未能检测到合成面孔可能会对安全和预防犯罪产生重要影响，因为超逼真的面具可能会导致一个人外表的关键特征被错误识别。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Stop thinking and start doing
paragraphs.translationZh: 停止思考并开始行动

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Most people have a dream in life, a vision of who or what they’d like to be in the future. At a minimum, everyone has interests and values that determine what they want out of their lives. Even so, trying to set achievable goals that you’ll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging. It can be hard to know where to even begin, and the things you hope to achieve may seem impossible. But, if you’re well prepared you may be able to set goals for your life that are just as fulfilling to work toward as to achieve.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 大多数人都有一个人生梦想，对未来想成为谁或做什么的愿景。至少，每个人都有兴趣和价值观，这些兴趣和价值观决定了他们想要从生活中得到什么。即便如此，尝试设定您将在多年内努力实现的目标可能会极具挑战性。甚至很难知道从哪里开始，而且您希望实现的目标似乎是不可能的。但是，如果您做好充分准备，您也许能够为自己的生活设定目标，这些目标在努力实现时和实现时一样令人满意。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) We all have goals that we want to achieve in our lives. These goals may include learning a new language, eating healthier and losing weight, becoming a better parent, saving more money, and so on. It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge. This is why we buy courses on how to start a business or how to lose weight fast or how to learn a new language in three months. We assume that if we knew about a better strategy, then we would get better results. We believe that a new result requires new knowledge.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 我们都有想要在生活中实现的目标。这些目标可能包括学习新语言、健康饮食和减肥、成为更好的父母、存更多的钱等等。人们很容易认为，你现在所处的位置与你未来想要达到的位置之间的差距是由于缺乏知识造成的。这就是为什么我们购买有关如何创业或如何快速减肥或如何在三个月内学习一门新语言的课程。我们假设，如果我们知道更好的策略，那么我们就会得到更好的结果。我们相信新的结果需要新的知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) What I’m starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results. In fact, learning something new can actually be a waste of time if your goal is to make progress and not simply gain additional knowledge.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 然而，我开始意识到，新知识并不一定会带来新结果。事实上，如果您的目标是取得进步而不是简单地获得额外的知识，那么学习新东西实际上可能是浪费时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) It all comes down to the difference between learning and practicing. Thomas Sterner, in his book The Practicing Mind, explains the key difference between practicing and learning. He says: “When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal.” Here the words “deliberate” and “intention” are key, because they define the difference between actively practicing something and passively learning it.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）这一切都归结为学习和实践之间的差异。托马斯·斯特纳（Thomas Sterner）在他的《实践思维》一书中解释了实践和学习之间的主要区别。他说：“当我们练习某件事时，我们会故意重复一个过程，以达到特定的目标。”这里“故意”和“意图”这两个词是关键，因为它们定义了主动练习某事和被动学习某事之间的区别。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results. Here are some additional ways to think about the difference. Let’s say your goal is to get stronger and more fit. You can research the best instructions on weight lifting technique, but the only way to build strength is to practice lifting weights. Let’s say your goal is to grow your startup. You can learn about the best way to make a sales pitch, but the only way to actually land customers is to practice making sales calls. Let’s say your goal is to write a book. You can talk to a best-selling author about writing, but the only way to become a better writer is to practice publishing consistently.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）学习新东西和练习新东西可能看起来非常相似，但这两种方法可能会产生截然不同的结果。以下是一些思考差异的其他方法。假设您的目标是变得更强壮、更健康。您可以研究有关举重技术的最佳说明，但增强力量的唯一方法是练习举重。假设您的目标是发展您的初创公司。您可以了解进行推销的最佳方法，但真正吸引客户的唯一方法是练习拨打销售电话。假设您的目标是写一本书。你可以与畅销书作家谈论写作，但成为更好的作家的唯一方法是坚持不懈地练习出版。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Passive learning creates knowledge. Active practice creates skill. Let’s consider a couple more reasons to prioritize active practice over passive learning. First, passive learning can be a stick that supports inaction. In many cases, learning is actually a way to avoid taking action on the goals and interests that we say are important to us. For example, let’s say you want to learn a foreign language. Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress (“Hey, I’m figuring out the best way to do this!”). Of course, you’re not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language).
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 被动学习创造知识。积极的练习创造技能。让我们考虑一下优先考虑主动练习而不是被动学习的几个原因。首先，被动学习可以成为支持不作为的大棒。在许多情况下，学习实际上是一种避免对我们认为重要的目标和兴趣采取行动的方法。例如，假设您想学习一门外语。阅读一本关于如何快速学习外语的书可以让你感觉自己正在取得进步（“嘿，我正在找出最好的方法来做到这一点！”）。当然，你实际上并没有练习能够实现你想要的结果（说外语）的行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In situations like this one, we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels. We make the mistake of being in motion rather than taking action. Learning is valuable until it becomes a form of procrastination (拖延) .
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在这种情况下，我们经常声称我们正在准备或研究最好的方法，但这些合理化让我们感觉自己正在前进，而实际上我们只是在白费力气。我们犯的错误是只在行动而不是采取行动。学习是有价值的，直到它变成一种拖延。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Another point to consider is that practice is learning, but learning is not practice. Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge, you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge. Active practice, meanwhile, is one of the greatest forms of learning because the mistakes you make while practicing reveal important insights.
paragraphs.translationZh: H）另一点需要考虑的是，实践就是学习，但学习不是实践。被动学习不是一种实践形式，因为尽管你获得了新知识，但你并没有发现如何应用这些知识。与此同时，积极的练习是最好的学习形式之一，因为你在练习时犯的错误揭示了重要的见解。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Even more importantly, practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge. You can watch an online course about how to build a business or read an article about a terrible disaster in a developing nation, but that knowledge is unproductive unless you actually launch your business or donate to those in need. Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 更重要的是，实践是利用你的知识做出有意义的贡献的唯一途径。您可以观看有关如何开展业务的在线课程，或阅读有关发展中国家发生的可怕灾难的文章，但除非您真正开展业务或向有需要的人捐款，否则这些知识毫无用处。学习本身对你来说很有价值，但如果你想对其他人有价值，那么你必须以某种方式表达你的知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The last important point to consider is that practice focuses your energy on the process. Thomas Sterner once said, “Progress is a natural result of staying focused on the process of doing anything.” The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day. When you realize this and begin to direct your focus toward practicing better habits day-in and day-out, continual progress will be the logical outcome. It is not the things we learn nor the dreams we visualize that determine our results, but rather the habits that we practice each day. Fall in love with boredom and focus your energy on the process, not the product.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 最后要考虑的重要一点是练习将你的精力集中在这个过程上。托马斯·斯特纳曾经说过：“进步是专注于做任何事情的过程的自然结果。”你现在的生活状态是你每天所练习的习惯和信念的结果。当您意识到这一点并开始将注意力集中在日复一日地养成更好的习惯上时，持续进步将是合乎逻辑的结果。决定我们结果的不是我们学到的东西，也不是我们想象的梦想，而是我们每天练习的习惯。爱上无聊，将精力集中在过程上，而不是产品上。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) What does this all mean? Is passive learning useless? Of course not. In many cases, learning for the sake of learning can be a beautiful thing. Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action. That said, the main point of this article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress. We often hide behind information and use learning as an excuse to delay the more difficult and more important choice of actually doing something. Spend less time passively learning and more time actively practicing. Stop thinking and start doing.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 这一切意味着什么？被动学习没有用吗？当然不是。很多时候，为了学习而学习可能是一件美好的事情。更不用说，当您决定采取行动时，吸收新信息可以帮助您做出更明智的决定。也就是说，本文的要点是学习本身并不会带来进步。我们经常隐藏在信息背后，并以学习为借口来推迟实际做某事的更困难和更重要的选择。少花时间被动学习，多花时间主动练习。停止思考并开始行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Acquisition of new knowledge may not guarantee the progress that you aim to make.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 获得新知识可能并不能保证你取得预期的进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Your current situation in life is built on the beliefs and habits you have been practicing daily.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 你目前的生活状况是建立在你每天所践行的信念和习惯的基础上的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Knowing the best way to learn a foreign language will not enable you to speak it without actual practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 知道学习外语的最佳方法并不能让你在没有实际练习的情况下说外语。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. People may find it demanding to create a goal which will take a long time to achieve.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39.人们可能会发现制定一个目标需要很长时间才能实现。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Learning and practicing seem to be very much alike, but the two processes can lead to quite different outcomes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 学习和实践似乎非常相似，但这两个过程可能会导致截然不同的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Absorbing new information is helpful in making better decisions prior to action.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 吸收新信息有助于在采取行动之前做出更好的决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Sometimes we may feel like we are making progress by doing some research or making preparations, but actually we are staying at the starting point.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 有时，我们可能会觉得通过做一些研究或做一些准备，我们正在取得进展，但实际上我们还停留在起点。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. We are inclined to think that a lack of knowledge prevents us from advancing to a better future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 我们倾向于认为缺乏知识会阻碍我们迈向更美好的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Learning can benefit you by itself, but only practice can turn what you learn into meaningful contributions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44、学习本身就可以使你受益，但只有实践才能将你所学到的转化为有意义的贡献。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Practice involves repeating a process intentionally to attain a particular objective.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 实践涉及有意重复一个过程以实现特定目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. Recent evidence points to drivers’ limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse. A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint. It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人车交互研究表明，即使是设计用于自动驾驶的系统也远非防错。最近的证据表明，驾驶员对这些系统能做什么和不能做什么的了解有限，这是导致系统滥用的一个因素。最近的一项研究从法律角度解决了过度信任司机以及由此导致的系统滥用问题。它着眼于自动驾驶汽车制造商应合法采取哪些措施，以确保驾驶员了解如何正确使用车辆。

paragraphs.sourceText: One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products. But this is far from ideal. The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications. Further, most end users don’t read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究中提出的一种解决方案是要求买家签署最终用户许可协议 (EULA)，类似于使用新软件产品时需要达成协议的条款和条件。但这远非理想。该协议可能无法向驾驶员提供足够的信息，导致对协议请求的性质及其影响感到困惑。此外，大多数最终用户不会阅读 EULA。 2017 年的一项研究显示，91% 的人无需阅读就同意这些观点。在年轻人中，97% 的人在没有查看条款的情况下就同意了。

paragraphs.sourceText: The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software. And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题在于，与使用智能手机应用程序不同，驾驶汽车存在严重的安全风险，无论驾驶员是人还是软件。人类驾驶员需要同意对软件和硬件的结果负责。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Warning fatigue” and distracted driving are also causes for concern. For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction. Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won’t fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction (发生故障) or an accident occur.
paragraphs.translationZh: “警告疲劳”和分心驾驶也令人担忧。例如，司机在收到连续警告后感到恼火，可能会决定忽略该消息。或者，如果在车辆行驶时显示该消息，则可能会分散注意力。考虑到这些限制和担忧，即使这种获得同意的模式得以推进，也可能无法完全保护汽车制造商在系统故障或发生事故时免于承担法律责任。

paragraphs.sourceText: Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase. Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions. All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自动驾驶车辆的驾驶员培训有助于确保驾驶员充分了解系统的功能和限制。这需要在车辆购买之外进行。最近的证据表明，即使依靠卖家提供的信息也无法回答很多问题。考虑到所有这些，自动驾驶汽车的前进之路毕竟不会一帆风顺。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 我们从人车交互研究中学到了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 要求买家签署最终用户许可协议有什么问题？

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. What would drivers do when they suffer from “warning fatigue”?
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 驾驶员出现“警告疲劳”时该怎么办？

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 对于继续要求买家签署最终用户许可协议，作者有何看法？

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations?
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 应该怎样做才能帮助驾驶员充分了解系统的功能和限制？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast, or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout? If so, you are likely among the millions of people in search of more protein-rich diets.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您是否曾经在早餐时混合过蛋白质饮料，或者在下午锻炼后吃过蛋白质棒？如果是这样，您可能就是数百万人中寻找富含蛋白质饮食的人之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Protein-enriched products are found everywhere. But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein, most Americans get twice as much as they need.
paragraphs.translationZh: 富含蛋白质的产品随处可见。但与所有人都需要更多蛋白质的宣传相反，大多数美国人摄入的蛋白质是他们需要的两倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts. Global retail sales of protein supplement products reached an astonishing U.S. $18.9 billion in 2020.
paragraphs.translationZh: 生活在最发达国家的许多人都相信食品公司和自认为健康专家制造的蛋白质缺乏的神话。 2020年全球蛋白质补充剂产品零售额达到惊人的189亿美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: But are we really in need of more protein? Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但我们真的需要更多蛋白质吗？美国的医生从未真正检查过蛋白质缺乏症的患者，因为只要每天摄入足够的热量，我们也很可能获得足够的蛋白质。

paragraphs.sourceText: In fact, Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine’s recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，美国人目前消耗的蛋白质几乎是美国国家医学院建议的每日蛋白质摄入量的两倍，尽管最理想的蛋白质摄入量可能因年龄和活动水平而异。

paragraphs.sourceText: For example, if you’re a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein. Generally, though, a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day, particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks of developing heart disease and cancer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，如果您是一名专注的运动员，您可能需要消耗更多的蛋白质。不过，一般来说，体重 140 磅的人每天摄入的蛋白质不应超过 120 克，特别是因为高蛋白饮食会使肾脏和肝脏功能紧张，并增加患心脏病和癌症的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然自一个多世纪前以来，脂肪和糖就轮流受到攻击，但蛋白质仍然是我们的最爱。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the 1970s through the 1990s, protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated (饱和的) fat consumption to heart disease.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从 20 世纪 70 年代到 90 年代，蛋白质产品仍然很常见，但在将糖和饱和脂肪摄入与心脏病联系起来的研究发表后，饮食焦点牢牢锁定在低热量、低脂肪、无糖休闲食品和饮料上，蛋白质产品有所回落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Later research in 2003, however, suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss, and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，后来 2003 年的研究表明，高蛋白饮食有助于减肥，并且蛋白质很快恢复了以前的营养超级巨星地位。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein. When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants (抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，大多数生活在高收入国家的人都消耗了足够的蛋白质。当我们用蛋白棒或饮料代替正餐时，我们还有可能错过真正食物中丰富的抗氧化剂（抗氧化）、维生素和许多其他益处。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. What do we learn about publicity over protein in America?
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 我们从美国对蛋白质的宣传中了解到什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency?
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 为什么美国的医生从未真正检查过蛋白质缺乏症患者？

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake?
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 在决定最优选的蛋白质摄入量时，人们应该考虑什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 一个多世纪以来，哪些食物基本上不再受欢迎？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.作者暗示发达国家的人们应该怎样做才能保持健康？

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，您有 30 分钟的时间将一段中文翻译成英文。您应该将答案写在答题卡 2 上。
